Subject: Private VPC - initial reference diagram and two integration questions

Neha / team,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood Dedicated options last week. Attached is a rough diagram our infra team sketched that shows where we expect to terminate egress, where the control-plane connector would live, and the minimal packet flows we care about. Two asks before the architecture review next week: 

1) Can Redwood's control plane run in our customer-managed control subnet (private) with only outbound TLS to a Redwood control endpoint (no inbound)? We want to avoid any inbound NAT rules on our firewall.

2) For the data plane (inference nodes), we need a recommended pattern for certificate rotation and trust bridging between our onprem KMS and Redwood's attestation — specifically for models & cache encryption keys.

Attached: vpc-reference-diagram-v1.svg (sketch)

If helpful, we can share a short runbook of our existing cert rotation cadence. Looking to confirm constraints so we can lock the topology before procurement.

— Rahul
Sr. Infra Eng, Novatech Systems

Subject: Re: Private VPC - initial reference diagram and two integration questions

Rahul — thanks for the diagram, looks clear. High level answers up front, below. We should still do a short architecture sync (30m) so we can annotate the diagram together. Can you confirm availability Wed or Thu?

Short answers:
- Control plane: Yes — Redwood supports an outbound-only control-plane connector pattern. We'll provide a small bootstrap agent that initiates TLS to our control endpoint and maintains a long-lived TLS session; no inbound firewall rules required.
- Data plane certs: We support an HSM/KMS-integrated key wrapping flow. Your onprem KMS can wrap short-lived DEKs (data encryption keys) that the node uses; for node attestation we recommend mTLS using node-identity certs provisioned via your internal CA and short-lived workload certs minted by Redwood's attestation service. We can document the exact API calls for rotation and automated renewal hooks.

I'm attaching our ops-playbook-draft-v0.9.pdf with recommended sequences for bootstrap, cert rotation, and emergency key revocation. Please review sections 2.3 and 3.1 (node bootstrap and cert rotation).

Proposed times: Wed 2026-06-17 09:00-09:30 PT or Thu 2026-06-18 11:00-11:30 PT. Which works for your team?

Action items if Wed: we'll produce an annotated diagram with control-plane NAT expectations and a small table of required firewall egress destinations/ports.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor

Quick technical notes / things I'll bring to the sync: 

- Control-plane TLS model: we expect to use mutual-TLS (client cert from the bootstrap agent) for the control channel. That gives us crypto-paired identity without requiring inbound NAT. The control endpoint FQDNs (we'll share a small list) should be whitelisted for outbound HTTPS.

- Data-plane KMS integration options: two modes — (A) KMS wraps DEKs (your preferred) and Redwood stores wrapped keys; node pulls wrapped key and unwraps locally with your KMS token; (B) Redwood-issued ephemeral keys stored in customer-provided HSM vault upon request. Mode A avoids any secret egress but requires a short-lived token exchange flow. We'll enumerate tradeoffs in the doc.

- Certificate rotation: recommend 7-day rotation for workload certs during early deployment; 30-day for node identity. We'll script automatic renewals via a sidecar process on the node.

I'll prepare an overlay of your diagram that marks the control-plane egress FQDNs and suggested tcp/udp ports.

-Aditya
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
